translations.text: After Moses, the Lord’s servant, died, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant, saying to him:
“Moses my servant has died. Now get up and cross the Jordan, you and all these people, into the land that I will give them.
Every place on which the soles of your feet tread I will give to you, just as I told Moses.
The wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates, and as far as the western sea where the sun sets, will be your territory.
No one will stand against you throughout your life. Just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you too. I will not abandon you or forget you.
Be strong and stand firm, for you will divide among these people the land that I swore to your ancestors I would give them.
So be strong and courageous, taking care to act as Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn away from these commands to the right or to the left, so that you may understand everything you do.

This book of the law must not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand how to do everything written in it. Your path will be straight, and the Lord will straighten all your paths. Then you will understand.
Look, I command you: stand firm and be courageous. Do not be discouraged or afraid, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua commanded the people’s scribes, saying to them:

“Go into the middle of the people’s camp and command the people, saying to them, ‘Prepare food for yourselves, because in three more days you will cross the Jordan and enter to take possession of the land that the Lord your God will give you.’”
And Joshua spoke to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, saying to them:
“Remember the word of the Lord that Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you, saying, ‘The Lord your God has given you rest and has given you this land.’

Let your wives, your children, and your livestock remain in the land that I gave you. But you must equip yourselves and cross ahead of your brothers. All of you who are able must equip yourselves and help them fight against them,

until the Lord your God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that the Lord our God will give them. Then each of you may return to his own inheritance, which Moses gave you on the side of the Jordan toward the sunrise.”
They answered Joshua, saying to him, “We will do everything you command us, and wherever you send us, we will go.
“Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you too. Only may the Lord our God be with you, just as he was with Moses.”
Anyone who will not submit to you and will not obey your words as you command him must die. Only be strong and courageous.”

And Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two young men from a place called Shittim to explore the land, saying to them, “Go up and explore the land, including Jericho.” The two young men set out, entered Jericho, and went into the house of a prostitute named Rahab, where they lodged.
The king of Jericho was informed, “Men from the people of Israel have come here tonight to spy out the land.”
The king of Jericho spoke to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who came into your house tonight, for they have come to spy out the land.”
The woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said to the king’s man, “It is true that the men came to me.
But when it grew dark and they were about to close the gate, the men went out and left. I do not know where they went. Hurry after them; perhaps you will catch them.”
But she had taken [?] up to her roof and hidden them under her flax, which was piled up on her roof.
The king’s men pursued them along the road leading to the Jordan, at the crossing places, and the gate was shut.
After their pursuers had gone out, and before the men had gone to sleep, Rahab went up to them on the roof.
She said to them, “I know that the Lord your God has given this land into your hands, for fear of you has fallen upon us, and the inhabitants of the land have lost courage before you.

For we heard that the Lord your God dried up the Red Sea before you when you came out of the land of Egypt, and what he did to the two Amorite kings who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed.
When we heard, our hearts melted, and no courage remained in any of us because of you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
Now then, swear to me by the Lord your God that, since I have shown you kindness, you too will show kindness to my father's household, and give me a trustworthy sign.
Keep my father's household alive, along with my mother, my brothers, my father's entire household, and everything they have, and save our lives from death.

The men said to her, "We will give our lives for yours, even to the point of death, if you do not disclose this matter of ours. And when the Lord gives this city into our hands, we will treat you with kindness and faithfulness."
She lowered them through her window.
She said to them, "Go to the mountain first, so that those pursuing you do not encounter you. Hide there for three days, until those pursuing you return, and afterward go on your way."
The men, the Israelites, said to her, "We are free of this oath.

Look, we are going to one side of the city. Set up this sign, this scarlet cord, and tie it to their window, through which you lowered us. Gather their father and [?] their mother and all their brothers into their house.
Anyone who goes outside the house will be responsible, and we will be free of this oath. Whoever is with you inside the house, we will keep alive.
But if you wrong us by disclosing our matter, we will be free of this oath."
She said to them, "Let it be so. The Lord be with you." She sent them away.
They went to the mountain first and stayed there for three days. Those pursuing them searched for them along all the roads but did not find them, and they returned to Jericho.
When they had returned, the two young men came down from the mountain, crossed over to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The Lord has given that entire land into our hands. All who live in that land are afraid of us."
When Joshua heard this, he rose early in the morning and had them set out from Shittim. [?] They came to the Jordan and stayed there until they crossed over.
After three days, the officers came out of the camp.
They instructed the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord our God, and the priests and Levites carrying it, leave your places and follow it.
But let there be a distance of two thousand cubits between us and it. Stand back and do not approach it, so that we will know the way you are to travel, for you have not traveled this way before."
Joshua said to the people, "Purify yourselves for tomorrow, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you."
Joshua said to the priests, "Carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord and walk ahead of the people." And [?] the priests carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord and walked ahead of the people.
The Lord said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you before all the Israelites, so that they will know that, just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you.
Now instruct the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, telling them, ‘When you enter the waters of the Jordan, stand in the Jordan.’"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here to me and listen to the word of the Lord our God."
By this you will know that the living God is powerful among you and will certainly drive out the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Amorites, the Girgashites, and the [?].
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will cross the Jordan ahead of you.
Now, then, choose twelve men from among you, from the people of Israel, one man from each tribe.
And when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth stand in the water of the Jordan, the water of the Jordan will divide, and the water flowing down will stop flowing.
The people set out from their camps to cross the Jordan, and the priests lifted the covenant onto themselves ahead of the people.

When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth reached the Jordan, and the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord first dipped into and became wet in part of the water of the Jordan—the Jordan was full of water, overflowing its entire bank, as in the days of the wheat harvest—

the water coming from upstream stopped flowing and stood firm, very, very far away, as far as the region of Kiriath-jearim. But the water flowing downstream ran out into the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, until it dried up completely. And the people were standing opposite Jericho.
The priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and all the Israelites crossed the Jordan on dry ground.
When all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying to him:
“Take men from among the people, one man from each tribe.

Command them to take twelve stones from this place in the middle of the Jordan, prepared and ready. Have them bring these, and set them down together at your campsite, the place where you will stay for the night.”
And when Joshua had called twelve men from among the people of Israel, one man from each tribe,

he spoke to them, saying, “Go ahead of me into the presence of the Lord, into the middle of the Jordan. Let each of you take a stone from that place and lift it onto his shoulder, according to the number of the twelve tribes of Israel.
So that these may be a sign for you, set up forever, and so that, when your son asks you in the future, saying, “What do these stones that have been set up mean to you?”

You too must open your son's eyes [?], saying to him, ‘Because the Jordan River dried up before the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth when it crossed.’ And these stones will be a memorial for you among the people of Israel forever.”

The people of Israel did these things as the Lord had commanded Joshua. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord had commanded Joshua. When all the people of Israel had finished crossing, they brought the stones with them up to their camp and set them down there.
Joshua also set up another twelve stones in the Jordan, in the place called “Beneath the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord.” They remain there to this day.
The priests carrying the ark of the Lord stood in the Jordan until Joshua had completed everything that the Lord had commanded him to tell the people. The people hurried, and all of them crossed.
When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the covenant of the Lord also crossed, and the stones were ahead of them.
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed, armed, ahead of the people of Israel, as Moses had commanded them.
About forty thousand people crossed in the presence of the Lord for battle against the city of Jericho.
From that day the Lord made Joshua great and exalted him before the entire nation of Israel. They feared him as they had feared Moses throughout his lifetime.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying to him:
“Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan.”
And Joshua commanded the priests, saying to them, “Come up out of the Jordan.”

And when the priests who carried the ark of the covenant came up out of the Jordan and stood on dry ground, the water of the Jordan flowed back into its own place and reached its banks as before, throughout the whole [?].
And all the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month. The Israelites camped at Gilgal, in its eastern part, opposite Jericho.
And Joshua set up at Gilgal these twelve stones that they had taken out of the Jordan,
saying to the Israelites, “When your children ask you in days to come, ‘What are these stones?’
you are to tell your children, saying to them, ‘Because Israel crossed the Jordan River on dry ground.’

The Lord our God dried up the water of the Jordan before Israel until they had all crossed it, just as the Lord our God did to the Red Sea, which the Lord our God dried up before us until we had crossed it.
So that all the nations of the earth may know that the Lord’s power is strong, and so that you yourselves may serve the Lord our God at all times.”

And when the kings of the Amorites who were on the bank of the Jordan, and the kings of the land of Phoenicia who were by the sea, heard that the Lord God had dried up the Jordan River before the Israelites as they crossed it, their hearts melted. They became weak, were overwhelmed, and were troubled, and no resolve at all remained in them before the Israelites.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua, “Make yourself stone knives from a high, sharp rock, and sit down and circumcise the Israelites a second time.”
And Joshua made himself sharp stone knives and circumcised the Israelites a second time. He left their foreskins at the place now called the Hill of Foreskins.
Now when Joshua circumcised the Israelites, those who had been born earlier on the journey and those who were uncircumcised among those who had come out of Egypt—
Joshua circumcised all of them, for Israel had spent forty years in the wilderness.

For this reason most of the warriors who had come out of Egypt were uncircumcised. They had not obeyed God’s commandments, and he declared concerning them that they would not see the land that the Lord had sworn to our ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
But in their place he raised up their children, whom Joshua circumcised, because they had been born on the journey and had not been circumcised.
After they were circumcised, they remained at rest, staying in the camp until they recovered.
And the Lord said before the people, “Today I have removed the disgrace of Egypt from you.” And he called that place Gilgal.
And the Israelites celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the western side of Jericho, on the bank of the Jordan, in the plain.
And they ate unleavened bread, fresh loaves made from the grain of the land.

On that day the manna ceased after they ate some of the grain of the land. There was no longer any manna for the Israelites, and they took possession of the territory of the people of Phoenicia that year.

And while Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing before him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua approached him and said to him, “Are you on our side, or do you belong to those who fight against us?”

He said to him, “I am the commander of the Lord’s army. I have come now.” And immediately Joshua fell facedown on the ground and bowed in worship. He said to him, “Lord, what do you command me, your servant?”
And the commander of the Lord’s army spoke to Joshua, saying to him, “Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was shut and secured. No one was coming out of it, and no one was going into it.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, I will hand Jericho over to you, along with its king who is in it, a man mighty in strength.
Station all the fighting men around it.
And when you blow the trumpet, let all the people shout together.
And when they shout, the walls of Jericho will fall down by themselves. Then all the people are to rush forward and go into the city, each one individually.”
And Joshua son of Nun went in to the priests.
He spoke to them, saying, “Command the people to go forward and march around the city, and let the fighting men march armed before the Lord.
And let seven priests, holding seven sacred trumpets, also march before the Lord, and let them keep sounding them. And let the ark of the Lord’s covenant follow them.
Let the fighting men go first and march in front, and let the priests who march behind the ark of the Lord’s covenant also blow their trumpets.”
Joshua commanded the people, saying to them, “Do not shout, and do not let anyone hear your voices until he himself tells you the day when you are to shout. Then you will shout.”
And when the ark of God’s covenant had gone around the city, it immediately returned to the camp and stayed there overnight.
And on the following day, the second day, Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests lifted the ark of the Lord’s covenant.

The seven priests who held the seven trumpets marched first before the Lord, and the fighting men marched after them. All the rest of the crowd followed the ark of the Lord’s covenant. The priests blew the trumpets, and the whole crowd together went around the city, on that side and on this side.
They returned again to the camp. This is what they did for six days.
And on the seventh day they rose early and went around the city six times.
On the seventh circuit, the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua said to the Israelites, “Shout loudly, for the Lord has handed the city over to you.

The city itself and everything in it are to be devoted to destruction for the Lord, dedicated to the Lord of hosts, Sabaoth. But spare Rahab the prostitute and everyone in her house, because she hid the spies whom we sent.

But you must be very careful to keep away from what is devoted to destruction, lest your hearts turn toward those things, or you take anything devoted to destruction and make the whole congregation of the Israelites an abomination and bring trouble upon us.
All silver, gold, bronze, and iron are to be consecrated to the Lord and brought into the Lord’s treasury.”

And the priests blew their trumpets. When the people heard the sound of those blowing the trumpets, all the people together raised a great, powerful shout. The entire wall around the whole city fell down, and all the people rushed straight ahead into the city, each one directly in front of him, and they took possession of the city.
They devoted it to destruction, along with everything in the city, from men to women, from young to old, and even cattle, sheep, and donkeys. They killed them all with the edge of the sword.
And Joshua said to the two young men who had explored the land, “Go into the woman’s house and bring her out of that place, along with everything that belongs to her.”

And the two young men who had explored the city entered the woman’s house and brought out Rahab the prostitute, her father, her mother, her brothers, her entire family, and everything she owned. They placed her outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city with fire, along with everything in it, except the silver and gold and all the bronze and iron, which they handed over to be brought into the Lord’s treasury.
Joshua kept Rahab the prostitute alive, along with her whole household and her father, and he let them live among the Israelites to this day, because Rahab had hidden those who explored Jericho.

And Joshua swore an oath that day before the Lord, saying, “Cursed is the man who rebuilds that city or lays its foundation. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest son he will set up its gates.” And this is what Oza of Bethel did: at the cost of Abiram, his firstborn, he laid its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest son who survived, he set up its gates.
And the Lord was with Joshua, and his name was famous throughout the whole land.

And the Israelites committed a great sin by taking and stealing some of the things devoted to destruction. Achar son of Carmi, son of Zimri, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of the things devoted to destruction and kept them back. And the Lord became fiercely angry with the Israelites.
And Joshua son of Nun sent men up to Ai, which is near Bethel, telling them, “Go and scout out Ai.”

And the men of Israel went up and scouted out Ai. They returned to Joshua and said to him, “Do not make all the people go up there. Instead, let two thousand or three thousand men go up and plunder the city. Do not make all the people go up there, for the city's people are few.”
And three thousand men went up, and they fled before the men of Ai.

And the men of Ai killed thirty-four of the Israelites. They pursued them from the gate and struck them down as far as the road leading downhill. And the people's hearts were shaken and melted like water.
And Joshua took hold of his clothes and tore them. Joshua fell facedown on the ground before the Lord until evening, together with the elders of Israel, and they scattered dust on their heads.

And Joshua pleaded with the Lord, saying, “I beg you, Lord, why did your servant—that is, I—bring this people across the Jordan to hand them over to the Amorites to destroy them? If only we had stayed on the other side of the Jordan and settled there!
And what can I say, since Israel has fled before its enemy?
When the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land hear about it, they will surround us and wipe us off the land. And what will we do for your great name?”
And the Lord said to Joshua, “Get up! Why have you fallen facedown on the ground like this?
The people have sinned and broken the covenant I established with them. They have stolen some of the things devoted to destruction and hidden them among their possessions.

The Israelites will not be able to stand and fight their enemies. They will turn back and flee before their enemies because they have become an abomination. I will no longer continue to be with you unless you remove the abomination from among you.

Get up and purify the people. Tell them to purify themselves for tomorrow, saying, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: There are things devoted to destruction among you. You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the things devoted to destruction from among you.’

And in the morning you are all to gather by tribes. The tribe that the Lord singles out you are to present by clans. The clan that the Lord singles out you are to present by households. The household that the Lord singles out you are to present man by man.
And the man whom the Lord singles out is to be burned with fire, together with everything he owns, because he has broken the Lord's covenant and committed a lawless act in Israel.”
And Joshua rose early in the morning and presented the people by tribes. And the Lord singled out the tribe of Judah.

He brought the tribe of Judah forward by clans, and the Lord singled out the clan of Zerah. He brought the clan of Zerah forward by households, and the Lord singled out the household of Zimri. He brought the household of Zimri forward one man at a time.
And the Lord singled out Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zerah.
Joshua said to Achan, “Give glory today to the God of Israel, and confess what you have done. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achan answered Joshua, saying, “I have truly sinned before the Lord, the God of Israel. This is exactly what I did:

I saw among the plunder a beautiful patterned cloak, two hundred staters of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty staters. When my heart desired them, I took them. They are lying hidden in the ground inside my tent, and the silver is buried beneath them.”
Joshua sent messengers after them, and they ran up to the tent in the camp. The things were lying in the tent, and the silver was beneath them.
They took them out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and the elders of Israel. They laid them down before the Lord.

Joshua took Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zimri, the son of Zerah, and brought him up to Pianahor [?], along with his sons and daughters, his calves and beasts of burden, all his sheep, and everything he owned. All Israel went with him, and he brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said to Achan, “Why have you destroyed us? The Lord will destroy you today.” And all Israel stoned him.
They piled a great heap of stones over him, and the Lord turned away from his fierce anger. For this reason he named that place the Valley of Achor, as it is called to this day.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or lose courage. Take all the fighting men with you, get up, and go up to Ai. Look, I have handed its king over to you, along with his city and the rest of his land.
You shall treat the city of Ai as you treated Jericho and its kingdom. You may take the livestock as plunder for yourself. But set an ambush against the city behind it.”
Joshua and all the fighting men got up to go up against Ai. Joshua heard [?] three thousand men who were strong and mighty, and sent them out at night.
He commanded them, saying, “You are to lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go too far from it, and all of you must be equipped and ready.
I and everyone with me will advance toward the city. When the inhabitants of Ai come out to meet us as they did before, we will flee before them.
When they pursue us, we will draw them away from the city. They will say, ‘Look, they are fleeing before us, defeated just as before.’
Then you must rise from the place where you are lying in ambush and enter the city.
Carry these things out according to these words. Look, I have given you your orders.”
Joshua sent them out, and they went up to the place where they would lie in ambush. He stayed between Bethel and Ai, on the western side of Ai.
Joshua rose early in the morning and inspected the people. He and the elders marched up ahead of the people toward the city of Ai.
All the fighting men went up with him. After marching, they came and took their position in front of the city, on its eastern side.
The men lying in ambush against the city remained on the western side.

When the king of Ai saw them, he immediately hurried out to meet them. He and his entire force with him took their positions against them for battle. But the king did not know that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.
When Joshua saw this, he and Israel retreated before them.
And the men of Ai set off in pursuit of Israel, moving away from the city.
Not a single person remained in the city of Ai who had not come out. They pursued Israel, leaving the city open, and followed after Israel.

And the Lord said to Joshua, “Stretch out your hand with the sword in it toward the city of Ai, for I have delivered the city into your hands. The troops lying in ambush will immediately rise from the place where they are hidden.” And Joshua stretched out his hand with his sword toward the city of Ai.

And the troops rose from the place where they were hidden and came out, because he had stretched out his hand toward the city. He sent them into the city, and they captured it and immediately set it on fire.
But the men of Ai looked behind them and saw the smoke of their city rising into the sky. They found nowhere to flee, either this way or that.

And Joshua and all Israel saw that the troops lying in ambush had captured the city and that the city's smoke was rising into the sky. Joshua and those with him turned back and struck down the men of the city of Ai.

And Israel's troops came out of the city and advanced against them. The men of Ai were caught in the middle of Israel's army, with some on one side of them and the others on the other side. They struck them down until they had left no one alive to escape or flee.
And they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him before Joshua.

And when the Israelites had finished killing all those who were in Ai, those in the plain and those on the mountain along the road descending to the place where they had pursued them, Israel returned to Ai and struck it down with the edge of the sword.
And those who fell that day, men and women alike, numbered twelve thousand, all inhabitants of Ai.
Except for the plunder in the city, which the Israelites took for themselves according to the Lord's command, just as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
And Joshua burned the city with fire and made it a permanent wasteland, uninhabited to this day.

And they hung the king of Ai on a tree with two crossbars, and he remained hanging on the tree until evening. As the sun was about to set, Joshua ordered his body to be taken down from the tree. He threw it into the pit, and they piled a great heap of stones over him, which remains to this day.

When the kings of the Amorites heard this—those on the bank of the Jordan, those in the mountains, those in the plain, those along the coast of the Great Sea, and those in the region of Lebanon—and the Hittites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Amorites, Girgashites, and Jebusites,
they gathered together to wage war against Joshua and all Israel.
Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

just as Moses, the Lord's servant, had commanded the Israelites, according to what is written in the law of Moses: to build an altar of whole stones on which no iron tool had been used. And there he offered a burnt offering to the Lord on it, and a peace offering.
And Joshua wrote on the stones Moses' Deuteronomy, which he wrote in the presence of the Israelites.

And all Israel, with their elders, leaders, and scribes, were moving along on either side of the ark, in front of it. The priests and the Levites stood carrying the ark of the Lord's covenant. Both the foreign resident and the native-born were there. Half of them were near Mount Gerizim, and the other half were near Mount Ebal, just as Moses, the Lord's servant, had commanded, to bless the people first.
And afterward Joshua read the words of this law, the blessings and the curses, according to everything written in the book of the law of Moses.

There was not a word among all that Moses had commanded Joshua that Joshua did not read aloud to the whole assembly of the Israelites—the men, the women, the little children, and the converts who traveled with Israel.
The inhabitants of the city of Gibeon heard about everything the Lord had done to Jericho and Ai.

They too acted cunningly. They set out and prepared [?], making them ready. They took old sacks and loaded them onto their necks, and old wineskins that were worn and torn; they filled them with wine and tied them up.

The soles of their shoes were worn through, and their other sandals were ragged, with patches fastened onto them around their feet. The clothes they wore were dirty and ragged, and the bread they had prepared was dry and moldy.
They set out and came to Joshua at Israel’s camp at Gilgal. They said to Joshua and Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us.”
Israel said to the Hivite, “Look, perhaps you live near me. How, then, can I make a covenant with you?”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”
They said to him, “We, your servants, have come from a very distant land in the name of the Lord your God, for we have heard of the name of the Lord your God and what he did in Egypt,
and what he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were on the other side of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.

Our elders and all the inhabitants of our lands instructed us, saying, ‘Take bread with you for the journey. Set out and go to him, and say to him, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’
We brought this bread with us while it was warm on the day we set out to come to you. Now it has dried out and crumbled because of the length of the journey.

We filled these wineskins when they were new, but they have split because of the long delay we experienced. Our clothes and shoes have worn out and become ragged on us because of the very long journey.”
The leaders took some of their bread from them without first consulting the Lord.
Joshua made peace with them, and they made a covenant with them to spare their lives. The leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
Three days after they made the covenant with them, they heard that they were not far away but lived nearby.
The Israelites set out and came to their cities. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
The Israelites did not fight against them, because all the leaders had sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. The whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
All the leaders said to the congregation, “We have sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. So now we cannot touch them.
Instead, this is what we will do for them: we will protect them and keep them alive, so that wrath does not come upon us because of the oath we swore to keep them safe.
They will be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” The whole congregation did as the leaders had told them.
Joshua summoned them and said to them, “Why did you deceive me by saying, ‘We live very far away,’ when you live nearby?
Now you are cursed. There will always be slaves and woodcutters among you to serve me and my God.”

They answered Joshua, saying, “We were told what the Lord God commanded through Moses his servant: to give you this land and wipe out everyone living on it before you. We were very afraid for our lives because of you, so we took action and did this.”
“Now look, we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good to you and whatever you wish.”
They treated them in this way: Joshua rescued them that day from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.

And on that day Joshua appointed them to cut wood and draw water for the whole assembly and for the altar of God. Thus the inhabitants of Gibeon became woodcutters and water carriers for the altar of God, to this very day, and for the place the Lord would choose to put his name there.

When Adoni-bezek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured the city of Ai and destroyed it, just as he had done to Jericho and its king, and as he had done to the city of Ai and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had gone over to Joshua and the Israelites,
they were very afraid of them, for he knew that Gibeon was a large city, like one of the very great cities, and all its men were strong men.
And Adoni-bezek, king of Jerusalem, sent word to Ailam, king of Hebron, to Philon, king of Jarmuth, to Jephthah, king of Lachish, and to Dabi, king of Adullam, saying to them,
“Get up and come up to me. Help me and fight against the city of Gibeon, for they have gone over to Joshua and the Israelites.”

And the five kings of the Jebusites came up—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Adullam—with all their forces. They camped against Gibeon and fought against it.

And the inhabitants of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at Israel’s camp in Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hand from your servants, who are we. Get up and come up to us quickly. Save us and help us, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
And Joshua got up and came up from Gilgal, with the entire force of fighting men accompanying him, each mighty in his strength.
And the Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over to you. Not a single one of them will survive before you.”
And Joshua came up against them suddenly, having traveled from Gilgal all night.

The Lord scattered them and threw them into confusion before the Israelites. And the Lord defeated them in a great slaughter at Gibeon. Joshua and Israel pursued them along the road going up to Beth-horon, and he struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled from the Israelites along the road coming down to Beth-horon, the Lord hurled hailstones down on them from heaven as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword in the battle.

Then he spoke to the Lord on the day when God handed the Amorites over to the Israelites, when he crushed them at Gabbathon and they were defeated before the Israelites. Joshua said, “Let the sun stand still over Gibeon, and the moon over the valley of Aijalon, until I [?] against these people.”
And the sun and the moon stood still in their course until God repaid the enemies. The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not move toward setting for a whole day.
And there had never been a day like this, either before or afterward, when God listened to a human being, for the Lord was helping Israel.
And these five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
And Joshua was told, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said to them, “Roll stones against the entrance of the cave, and station men there to guard them.
But you must not stop pursuing your enemies. Catch their rear guard and do not let them enter their cities, for the Lord our God has handed them over to you.”
And when Joshua and the Israelites had finished striking them down in a very great slaughter, completely, those who had escaped made it safely into the fortified cities.
All the people returned to Joshua at Makkedah, all of them safe. None of the Israelites uttered a sound with his tongue.
Joshua said to them, “They have opened this cave. Bring these five kings out of the cave.”
They brought the five kings out of the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Adullam.

They brought them out before Joshua. Joshua called all Israel and the commanders of the army who had gone with Joshua. He said to them, “Go and put your feet on the necks of these kings and kill them.” The men went and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, “Do not be afraid, but be victorious and strong, for this is what the Lord God will do to your enemies whom you will fight.”
Joshua killed them and hung them on five trees until evening.

After sunset, Joshua gave orders, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had fled. They rolled a hundred stones against the entrance of the cave, which remain to this day.

They captured Megiddo that day and killed everyone in it with the sword. They destroyed everyone who breathed in it. No one remained alive or escaped from it. They treated the king of Megiddo as [?] the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Megiddo to Libnah and surrounded it.

The Lord gave it into Israel’s hands. They captured it and its king with the sword and destroyed everyone who breathed in it. No one remained alive or escaped from it. They treated its king as they had treated the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Libnah to Lachish. He camped beside it and surrounded it.
The Lord gave Lachish into the hand, into the hand of Israel. On the second day they captured it with the sword, and he wiped it out as he had done to Libnah. [?] Elam
the king of Gezer, to help Lachish. Joshua struck him and his army with the sword, leaving none of them alive or able to escape.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Lachish to Adullam. They camped beside it and surrounded it.
The Lord gave it into Israel’s hands. They captured it with the sword and killed everyone who breathed in it, as they had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went to Hebron.
He destroyed it with the sword, along with every living thing in it. No one in it survived, just as he had done to Adullam, wiping out its inhabitants.
Joshua and all Israel turned toward Debir and camped beside it.

They captured it, along with its king and its villages, and destroyed it and every living thing in it, leaving no survivor, just as he had done to Hebron and its king, and just as he had done to Debir and its king.

Joshua struck the whole region: the hill country, the high land, the western land, the plain, the land in between, and Ashdoth, together with its kings. They left none of them alive, and they wiped out everything that had the breath of life, as the Lord God had done, as far as Kadesh-barnea.
From Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza, all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their lands one after another, because the Lord God was fighting for Israel.
When Abis, the king of Hazor, heard, he sent to Jobab, the king of Merom, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Ziph,
and to the kings near Greater Sidon, in the hill country, the high land, in the Arabah opposite Chinnereth, in the plain, the land in between, and in Naphoth-dor,
and to the Canaanites on the coast to the east, and to the Amorites on the other coast, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites in the mountains, and the Hittites in the mountains, at Shechem.
They all came out with their other kings accompanying them, as numerous as the sand of the sea, with very many horses and chariots.
And all these kings assembled together and came to the waters of Merom to wage war against Israel.
And the Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for at this time tomorrow I will hand them over, slain before Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
And Joshua came with all the fighting men against them suddenly at the waters of Merom. He rushed against them in the hill country, the highlands.

And the Lord handed them over to Israel. They struck them down and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon, as far as Misrephoth-maim, and as far as the plains of Lon to the east. They struck them down until they had left no survivor behind.
And Joshua did to them as the Lord had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
And Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor and its king. Hazor had formerly ruled over all these kingdoms.
And they killed everything in it that had the breath of life with the edge of the sword. He destroyed them all, and they left none of them behind. They burned Hazor with fire.
And Joshua captured all the other cities of the kings and their other kings. He killed them with the edge of the sword and destroyed them, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, the Lord’s servant.
But Israel did not burn any of the cities built on mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

And the Israelites took all its plunder for themselves, but they destroyed all the people. He utterly destroyed them, one after another, with the edge of the sword, leaving none of them with the breath of life.
Just as the Lord had commanded Moses, Moses in turn commanded Joshua. He left undone none of all the things Moses had commanded him.

And Joshua captured the highlands, all the land of the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the plain—the land in between—the land to the west, the mountain of Jerusalem, and the other places in between, or

those on the side of the mountain, from Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad and as far as the plain of the land of Lebanon at Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, destroyed them, and killed them.
And Joshua spent many days waging war against all these kings.
There was not a single city that the Lord did not hand over to the Israelites. He captured them all in war.

For this decree came from the Lord, to harden their hearts so that they would come out to wage war against Israel, so that they would be destroyed and shown no mercy, but would be utterly destroyed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

And Joshua came at that time and wiped out the Anakim from the hill country, the highlands, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anaboth, from Aboth, and from the whole mountain region of Judah, along with their other cities. Joshua destroyed them.
None of the Anakim remained among the Israelites, except in Gaza and in Ashdod; these were the places where they remained.
And Joshua captured the whole land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Joshua gave the land to Israel as an inheritance, dividing it according to its tribes. And the land rested from war.

And these are the kings of the land whom the Israelites killed and whose land they inherited on the eastern side of the Jordan, from this side of the Arnon as far as the mountain, the land of Hermon, and all the land of the Arabah east of Seir:
the kings who were from Sidon, who ruled from the Arnon, which is in the valley, over a portion of the valley and half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok, the borders of the Ammonites;
And the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward along the road leading up to Jeshimoth, from the south below [?] Pisgah.
and Og, the king of Bashan, who remained from among the giants and lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei.
He ruled from Mount Hermon and from Salecah, and over all Bashan as far as the boundaries of the Girgashites, Maacah, and half the territory of Gilead, the territory of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses, the Lord’s servant, and the Israelites struck them down. And Moses gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

And these are the kings of the Amorites whom Moses and the Israelites killed on the other side of the Jordan, beside the sea of Baal-gad in the plain of the land of Lebanon, as far as Mount Halak, going up toward Seir. Joshua gave that land to the tribes of Israel to inherit according to their allotted shares.

And in the mountains of the highlands, in the plain of the central region, in the Arabah, in Ashdoth, in the wilderness, and in the Negev: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites.
And the king of Jericho, and the king of Ai, which is near Bethel.
The king of Jerusalem; the king of Hebron.
The king of Jarmuth; the king of Lachish.
The king of Eglon; the king of Gezer.
The king of Debir; the king of Gaisei.
The king of Hormah; the king of Arad.
The king of Libnah; the king of Adullam.
The king of Makkedah.
The king of [?]; the king of Hepher.
The king of Aphek; the land of Hazor.
The king of Asom.
The king of Shimron; the king of Meron; the king of Achshaph.
The king of Kedesh; the king of Taanach.
The king of Megiddo; the king of Hierokom.
The king of Dor; the king of Goiim, in the land of Galilee.
The king of Tirzah. All the kings numbered twenty-six.
Joshua had grown old and was advanced in years. The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, you have grown old, and much land still remains to be inherited.
And this is the land that remains: the territories of the Philistines, the Geshurites, and the Canaanites,

from the uninhabited land facing Egypt as far as the borders of Ekron to the north. These are counted as belonging to the Canaanites: the five territories ruled by the Philistines—the people of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and the Hivites—
in Teman, and Ekron, and all the land of Canaan opposite, from Gaza, and the territory belonging to Sidon, as far as Aphek, as far as the borders of the Amorites;
and all the land of Galabiath belonging to the Philistines, throughout all the land of Lebanon, from the east as far as Gilgal at the foot of Mount Hermon, as far as the road leading into Hamath.
All who live in the hill country, the highlands, from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim—all the Sidonians—I myself will drive them out before Israel, just as I commanded you.

Now divide this land among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh. You are to give it to them from the Jordan as far as the Great Sea toward the west. The Great Sea itself will be the boundary.
To the two tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh, those who are with Reuben and Gad, Moses gave land on the other side of the Jordan toward the east. Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave it to them,
from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon ravine, and the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plain from Medeba.
All the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the borders of the Ammonites.
And all the land of Gilead, the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all Mount Hermon, and all the land of Bashan as far as Elcha.
The whole kingdom of Og in the land of Bashan, who reigned in Edrei and Ashtaroth and was left from the giants. Moses struck him down and destroyed him.
But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites, the Maacathites, or the Canaanites. The king of Geshur and the Maacathites have lived among the Israelites to this day.

Only the tribe of Levi was given no inheritance, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as the Lord told them. This is the division of the land that Moses divided among the Israelites on the plains of Moab, on the other side of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
And Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Aroer, opposite the Arnon valley, including the city in the Arnon valley and all the land of the plateau,
as far as Heshbon, and all the cities on the plateau, including Dibon and Bamoth,
and Maabalassa, Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
and Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Serada, and Sion on Mount Enab,
and Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plateau and the entire kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, whom Moses struck down, along with the leaders of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the ruler of [?], who lived in Sihon.
And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, was killed in the war.
The territory of Reuben reached the Jordan, which formed their boundary. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Reuben according to their clans, with their cities and villages.
Moses also gave land to the descendants of Gad according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer, that is, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Arad, opposite Arabah,
And from Heshbon down to Araboth, by the cities of Arad, and again from Heshbon down to Araboth opposite Mizpah, and from Mizpah to Betonim, and from Maam to the boundaries of Dibon.

and Enadaim, Petharcai, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. The Jordan was to form the boundary as far as part of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the eastern side of the Jordan.
This was the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans, with their cities and their other villages.
Moses also gave land to half the tribe of Manasseh according to their clans.
And their boundaries extended from Mana, including the whole kingdom of Bashan and the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in the land of Bashan—sixty cities.
He gave half the land of Gilead, together with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of Og’s kingdom in the land of Bashan, to the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh, according to their clans.
These are the lands that Moses gave them as an inheritance on the other side of the Jordan, on the plains in the land of Moab, on the eastern side of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.

These, in turn, are the lands that the Israelites inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave them as an inheritance.
They received their inheritance according to their clans, just as the Lord had commanded through Joshua, for the nine tribes and half the tribe of Manasseh,
from the other side of the Jordan. And he gave the Levites no inheritance among them.

For the descendants of Joseph formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites were given no share of the land, but only cities to live in and the surrounding fields assigned to them and their livestock.
The Israelites did just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they divided the land among themselves.
The descendants of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know what the Lord said to Moses, the man of God, about me at Kadesh-barnea.”
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of God, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land, and I brought him a report in keeping with his heart.
But my brothers who went up with me discouraged the people, while I devoted myself to following the Lord my God.
Moses swore that day, saying, “The land you entered will be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you devoted yourself to following the Lord your God.”

And now our Lord has kept me alive, just as he said. This is the fortieth year since the day when the Lord spoke these words to Moses, while Israel traveled in the wilderness. Now look: today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was when Moses first sent me. Even now I am able to go out to war and return.

So now I ask you for this mountain, just as the Lord said that day, because you yourself heard these words that day. Now the cities among the Anakim are large and fortified. If the Lord is with me, I will drive them out, just as the Lord told me.
Joshua blessed him and gave the city of Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh, son of Kenaz, as an inheritance.
For this reason, the city of Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh, son of Kenaz, as an inheritance to this day, because he followed the command of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Hebron was formerly called the city of Argob. It was the great city of the Anakim. And the land rested from war.
The territory of the tribe of Judah, according to their clans, extended from the borders of Idumea, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Kadesh, on the western side.
Their boundaries extended from the west to a section of the Salt Sea, from the mountain ridge that rises toward the west.

The boundary extends to the road going up to Akrabbim, continues out to Axenachim, and goes up from the west above Kadesh-barnea. It goes out to Hezron and Addar, and comes up above Kadesh toward the places where the sun sets.
And it goes down to Selmona and extends to the stream of Egypt, and its boundary ends at the sea. These are their boundaries on the west.
Their eastern boundary was the Salt Sea as far as a section of the Jordan. Their boundary went up toward the north, from the high mountain ridge by the sea and from a section of the Jordan.
Their boundary goes up to Beth-hoglah and extends from the north up to Beth-arabah. The boundary goes up to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

The boundary goes up to the foot of the mountain of the Valley of Achor and comes up to Gilgal, which faces the ascent of Adummim, west of the valley. It goes out to the water of the Spring of the Sun, and its endpoint is the spring of En-rogel.

The boundary goes up to the Valley of Hinnom, south of Jebus on its western side—that is Jerusalem. The boundary extends out to the mountain ridge facing the Valley of Hinnom by the sea, at the northern edge of the land of the Rephaim.
The boundary extends from the mountain peaks to the spring, the waters of [?], and goes out to Mount Ephron. The boundary reaches Jebaal, which is the city of Jearim.
The boundary turns around Baal toward the sea and comes down to Mount Seir, alongside the city of Jearim on the north—that is Chesalon. It reaches the City of the Sun and turns west.
The boundary extends alongside Ekron to the north. The boundary extends down to Socoh, goes out toward the west, and extends to Lemna. The endpoint of the boundary reaches the sea.
Their boundary will be the Great Sea, which marks the boundary. These are the boundaries surrounding the descendants of Judah, according to their clans.
And he gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a share among the descendants of Judah, according to God's command. Joshua gave him Arba, the great city of Anak, which is Hebron.
Caleb son of Jephunneh drove out from that eastern region the three daughters of Anak: Sheshai, [?] Talmai, and Ahiman.
Caleb went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir was formerly called the City of Writings.
And Caleb said, “Whoever captures the City of Writings and destroys it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured the city, and he gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
As she was coming out, he advised her, saying, “Ask your father for a field.” She cried out from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, “Why are you crying out?”
She said to him, “Give me a blessing, because you have assigned me to the land of the Negeb, a distant land. Give me Baiththianis.” And he gave her Gon aithlaam, which is below.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Judah.
Their cities were: the first city of the tribe of the descendants of Judah, on the border of Edom in the wilderness, and Beseleelin, and Ara and Hazor;
and Igma and Regma, and Aruel;
and Kadesh, and Asorinonaim, and Meman;
and Balmath, with their villages;
and the city of Hezron, which is Hazor;
and Shem and Asalma, and Moladah;
and Sergarei, and Beth-pelet;
and Chola, and Seola and Beersheba, and their villages, and their cities or their outlying settlements;
Balak, and Akok, Asom;
and Eltolad, and Bethel and Hormah;
and Seladad and Macharim, and Sethenna;
and Pelabos, and Salo and Eremoth: twenty-five cities with their villages.
In the plain, the land in the middle: Eshtaol and Zorah, and Essa;
and Heramme, and Zanoah and Jarmuth;
and Adullam and Lemera, and Socoh and Azekah;
and Shaaraim and Dargera, with their outlying settlements: fourteen cities with their villages.
Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-gad;
and Dilean, and Massia and Joktheel.
And Lachish, Bozkath, and Eglon,
and Cabbon, and Machoes, and Galenos,
And Gederoth, Bagadiel, Naamah, and Makkedah—sixteen cities with their villages.
Libnah and Iathakanoch,
and Janah and Nasim,
and Keilah, and Amehei, and Achzib, and Mareshah, and Elom: fifteen cities with their villages.
Ekron with its villages and their outlying settlements.
From Ekron, Jeremna, and the other places, or all the other cities near Ashdod, with their other villages.
Ashdod with its villages and its other outlying settlements, as far as the torrent, the watercourse of Egypt; and the Great Sea itself will form their boundary.
And in the hill country, the highlands: Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh,
And Renna, the city of writings, which is Debir.
and Anor, and Eshtemoa, and Aisam,
and Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh: eleven cities with their villages.
Erem, Remna, and Soma,
and Janum, and Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah,
and Euah, and the city of Arba, which is Hebron, and Zior: nine cities with their outlying settlements.
And Maon, and Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah,
and Ariel, and Arikam, and Senakim,
and Gibeah, and Timnah: nine cities with their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor,

and Maarath, and Beth-anoth, and Eltekon: six cities with their other villages. (a) a Tekoa and Ephrathah, which is Bethlehem, and Peor, and Etam, and Coulom, and Tatan, and Sobes, and Kee, and Gallim, and Theer, and Manocho: eleven cities with their other villages.
Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, and Sotheba: two cities with their outlying settlements.
Dabdabargis, Tharabam, and Maron,
and Sochoza, and Naphlazo, and Sodom, and En-gedi: seven cities with their other villages.
As for the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, the people of Judah could not destroy them, and the Jebusites have lived in Jerusalem to this day.

The boundaries of the descendants of Joseph began at the Jordan opposite Jericho, on the east. They will go up from Jericho into the hill country, into the wilderness, the highlands, up to Bethel, Luz.
And they will go out to Bethel, and they will extend to the boundaries of Ekron.
And they will pass toward the sea, along the boundaries of Aptalim, as far as the boundaries of Lower Beth-horon, and their endpoint will be at the sea.
And Joseph’s descendants, Ephraim and Manasseh, received their inheritance according to their clans.
The boundaries of their inheritance on the eastern side were Ataroth and Orek, as far as Upper Beth-horon and Gezer.
And the boundaries will pass toward the sea, down to Icathmon. From north of Thergam they will cross eastward to Thenasa and Sellessa, and they will pass from the east down to Nanotha.
And down to Maracho and Ataroth with their villages. They will extend from Jericho and stretch out from the Jordan.
And from Tappuah the boundaries extend toward the sea and to Kanah, and they end at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.
And the cities that were set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all the cities with their villages.

And Ephraim did not destroy the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. They lived with Ephraim to this day, until Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, came up, captured it, and burned it with fire. He destroyed the Canaanites and the Perizzites who lived in Gezer, and Pharaoh gave it as a dowry to his daughter.

The boundaries of the tribe of Manasseh’s descendants were established, because he was Joseph’s firstborn: Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn, the father of Gilead—for they were warriors in the land of Gilead and the land of Bashan.

And they belonged to the remaining descendants of Manasseh according to their clans: the descendants of Jedur, the son of Caleb, the descendants of Jeriel, the descendants of Shechem, the descendants of Soumarim, and the descendants of Hepher. These were the male descendants according to their clans.
And Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, had no sons, only daughters. These are the names of Zelophehad’s daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they stood before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua, and before the leaders, saying, “God commanded through Moses that we should be given an inheritance among our brothers.” And according to the Lord’s command, they were given a share among their father’s brothers.
And the measuring line of their territory extended from Asa and the field of Maaleah, apart from the land of Gilead, which is on the bank of the Jordan.
Because the daughters of Manasseh’s descendants inherited an allotment among their brothers. But the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining descendants of Manasseh.
And the boundaries of Manasseh’s descendants were Delanad, which is opposite the descendants of Onath. They proceed along the boundaries to Jamin and down to Jasib, at the spring of Tappuah.
They will belong to Manasseh, but Tappuah, on Manasseh’s boundary, will belong to the descendants of Ephraim.

And the boundaries will descend to the valley of Karana, westward, opposite the valley of Nariel, the terebinth tree and the descendants of Ephraim [?], in the middle of the city of Manasseh, northward down to the torrent. Its endpoint will be the sea.
From the west of Ephraim and along the north of Manasseh, the sea itself will be their boundary. They will adjoin Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

And Manasseh will have, within Issachar and Asher, Beth-shean with its villages, the inhabitants of Dor with its villages, the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages, and the third part of Maphedan with its villages.
The descendants of Manasseh were unable to drive out these cities, and the Canaanites would come to settle in this land.
And when the descendants of Israel became strong, they rose against the Canaanites and subdued them, but they did not drive them out completely.

But Joseph’s descendants stood before Joshua and said to him, “Why have you assigned us only one allotment as an inheritance and given us only one measured portion as an inheritance? I am a numerous people, and God has blessed me.”
Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear it for yourself, if the city of Ephraim is too small for you.”

They said to him, “The hill country of Ephraim will not be enough for us, and the Canaanites who live in Beth-shean and its villages, in the valley of Israel, have fine horses and a great deal of iron.”
And Joshua said to the descendants of Joseph, “Since you are a numerous people and have great strength, you will not have only one allotment.”
“And you will clear it, and it will be counted as yours. And if you drive out the Canaanites with choice horses—for they have many of them—you are stronger than they are.”
And the whole assembly of the people of Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the Lord’s tent of testimony there. And the land

And when the men got up, they set out. Joshua instructed the men who were going to survey the land, saying to them, “Go and survey the land according to its boundaries, and return to me. Here in Shiloh I will cast lots for you before the Lord.”
And they went and surveyed the land, examined it carefully, and recorded its boundaries in a book, city by city, in seven portions. They brought it to Joshua at Shiloh.
And Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the Lord.
And the allotment of the tribe of Benjamin came out first, according to their clans. The boundaries of their allotment lay between Judah and the descendants of Joseph.

And their northern boundary began at the Jordan. Their boundary goes up behind Jericho on the north and goes up into the mountains toward the sea. Its endpoint is the place called the wilderness of Beth-aven.
And from there the boundary turns toward Luz, behind Luz on the west—that is Bethel. The boundary goes down to the place called [?], to Arothorek, down to the hill country west of Lower Beth-horon.

And the boundary turns and bends around the place that faces the sea on the west. Its endpoint is Kiriath-baal—that is Kiriath-jearim, the city of the people of Judah. This is the side facing the sea.
And the side facing west begins at the outskirts of Kiriath-baal. The boundary bends down to the place called Gazein, to the spring of Nephtoah.

And the boundary goes down to a region opposite the place of [?] Hinnom, which lies north of the region of Rephaim. It goes down to the place called Hinnom, [?] of the Jebusites. And from the north it goes down to the spring of En-rogel.

And the boundaries will pass to the spring of Beth-shemesh and turn toward the place called Geliloth, which is opposite the road going up to Adummim. They will descend to the stone of Bohan, of the descendants of Reuben.
And they will turn along the edge of Beth-arabah on the north and descend.
Along the boundary behind the sea on the north, the endpoint of the boundary extends to the high inlet of the Salt Sea on the north, to a section of the Jordan on the west.
And the Jordan forms the boundary on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the people of Benjamin, with its surrounding boundaries, according to their clans.
And the cities of the people of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, and Amergasis,
and Beth-arabah, Nambra, and Beth-shan,
and Aiim, Parah, and Euratha,
and Carpha, Chephirah, Moni, and Geba: twelve cities with their villages.
And Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth,
and Massema, Biron, and Tamoke,
and Chepharaa, Caphan, Nacan, Cersea, and Selasec,
and Jebus—that is Jerusalem—and Bamoth-jearim: thirteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the people of Benjamin according to their clans.
And the second lot came out for the people of Simeon according to their clans. Their inheritance lay within that of the people of Judah.
And their allotment was Beersheba, Shema, and Coladaam,
and Arsola, Bola, and Iason,
and Elthula, Bula, and Hormah,
and Ziklag, Benthachebeb, and Sarusim,
and Batharoth with their fields: thirteen cities with their villages.
Rimmon, Thalc, Ether, and Ashan: four cities with their villages,
which surround these cities as far as Balek, going down to Jeneth on the west. This is the inheritance of the people of Simeon according to their clans.

The inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans, comes from Judah's allotment. These are the boundaries of the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans. These are the boundaries of the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, taken from Judah's allotment, because the portion of the descendants of Judah was too large for them. So the descendants of Simeon received their inheritance within Judah's allotment.
And the third lot came out for Zebulun, according to their clans. The boundaries of their inheritance will extend to Sedekgola, their boundary.
And the sea and Margela; and they will reach Beth-arabah, down to Pia, which is opposite Jokneam.
And they will turn toward Sedduk, opposite the eastern side of Beth-shemesh, to the boundaries of Chaselothaiai. They will pass to Daberath and go up to Naphar.
And from there they will turn eastward toward Gath, toward the city of Kasei, and will pass on to Rimmon, Amathar, and Aoza.
And the boundaries will turn northward toward Amoth, and their endpoint will be at Gephel.
And Kattath and Nahalal and Shimron and Jidalah and Bethlehem.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun, according to their clans: their cities and their villages.
And Issachar's lot came out fourth.
And their boundaries were Jazer and Chesulloth and Shunem.
And Arin and Senna and Reetha and Anaharath.
And Daberath and Kishion and Ebez.
And Hermmas and Ieon and Beth-pazzez.
And their boundaries will reach Thaithom and Salem toward the sea, and Beth-shemesh. And the endpoint of its boundaries is the Jordan.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar, according to their clans: their cities and their villages.
And the lot for Asher came out fifth.
And their boundaries were Eleleketh and Alek and Bethok and Achshaph.
And Elimelech and Amiel and Maasa; and it will reach Carmel toward the sea, and Shihor and Libnath and San.
And it will turn eastward, and to Bethaigeneth, and reach Zebulun and Iphthahel, and toward the sea on the north. The boundaries will pass to Saphta, Bethek, and Neiel, and turn down to Chobamasomel.
And Hebron and Raaph and Emmaon and Kanthan, as far as Greater Sidon.

And the boundaries will turn toward Ramah and as far as the spring of Masphassat and the territory of Tyre. And the boundaries will turn toward Iaseph, and its endpoint is the sea, and from Leb and Achzib.
And Archob and Aphek and Hraak.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Asher, according to their clans: their cities and their villages.
And Naphtali's lot came out sixth.
And their boundaries were Moolam and Molai and Besemiein and Karmai and Nabok and Jephthan, as far as Dodan. And the endpoint of its boundaries is the Jordan.

And its boundaries will turn toward the sea, to the territory of Tabor, and will pass from there to Aika. And they will reach Zebulun on the south, and it will reach Asher on the side toward the sea. And the Jordan will be on the east.
And the cities belonging to Tyre are cities surrounded by walls: Tyre and Omaatha and [?] and Chinnereth.
and Armath and Arahel and Hazor
and Kedesh and Sarae and the spring of Hazor.
And Keroth, Magalaarim, Betham, and Beth-shemesh.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali.
And the seventh lot fell to Dan.
And their territory included Zorah and Asa, the city of Samus,
And Shaalabbin, and [?], and Ithlah.
and Aijalon and Timnah and Ekron,
And Eltekeh, and Gibbethon, and Baalath.
And Hazor, and Bene-berak, and
and those from the sea of those called Hierakon, the mountain near Joppa.

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan [?], according to their clans, their cities and their other villages. (a) And the descendants of Dan did not subdue the Amorites, who were oppressing them in the hill country. The Amorites would not let them come down into the plain, and kept them confined within the boundaries of their allotted territory.

And the descendants of Dan went and fought against the city of Lamech. They captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword. They settled in it and called it Lasendak. (a) And the Amorites continued to live in Aijalon and Shaalbim, and Ephraim's power grew strong over them.
And they went to survey the land and their boundary. And the descendants of Israel gave Joshua son of Nun an allotted inheritance among them,
at God's command. And they gave him the city he had asked them for, namely Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim. He built the city and settled in it.

These are the portions that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave as an inheritance, according to their lots, at Shiloh before the Lord, beside the entrance of the tent of testimony.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Speak to the descendants of Israel and say, ‘Designate cities as places of refuge, the ones I spoke about through Moses,
a place of refuge for the killer who has killed someone unintentionally. These cities will be places of refuge for you,
so that the person who kills will not die at the hand of the avenger of blood,
until he stands before the assembly to be judged.’”
And he set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali, and the city of Arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

And on the other side of the Jordan he designated the city of Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; the city of Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and the city of Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These are the cities that the descendants of Israel designated, also for the foreigner living among them, so that anyone who killed someone unintentionally could flee to them and not die at the hand of the avenger of blood until he stood before the assembly that would judge him.
The leaders of [?] came forward.
And the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and the lands belonging to them by lot, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
And the tribe of the descendants of Judah, the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, and the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin gave them these cities and named them
as belonging to the descendants of Aaron from the clan of Kohath among the descendants of Levi, because the lot fell to them.
And they gave them the city of Kiriath-arba, the great city among the cities of Anak—that is, Hebron—in the hill country of Judah, together with the lands belonging to it all around.
And Joshua gave the city's fields and its villages to the descendants of Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.

And to the descendants of Aaron he gave the city of refuge for someone who had killed a person—that is, Hebron—and the city of At[?] with its surrounding lands, and the city of Libnah with its surrounding lands.
And the city of Ailon with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Tame with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Tella with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Debir with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Ashan with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Beth-shemesh with the other lands belonging to it: nine cities from these two tribes, and from these tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin, the city of Gibeon with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Gethe with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Anathoth with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Gamala with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.
All the cities of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, amounted to thirteen cities.
And the clans of the descendants of Kohath, the Levites who remained from among the descendants of Kohath—and the priestly city was from the tribe of Ephraim.

And they gave them the city of refuge for someone who had killed a person: the city of Shechem with the other lands belonging to it; also the city of Gezer with the other lands belonging to it, the city of Gethban with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Kibzaim with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Beth-horon with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Beth-horon with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.
And from the tribe of Dan, the city of Eltekeh with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Gibbethon with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Aijalon with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Gath-rimmon with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.
And from the tribe of Manasseh, the city of Nanach with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Bethara with the other lands belonging to it: two cities.
All the cities amounted to ten, together with all the other lands belonging to them, for the clans of the descendants of Kohath who remained.

And to the descendants of Gershon, the Levites, they gave, from the half-tribe of Manasseh, one of the cities set apart for those who had killed someone: the city of Golan in the land of Bashan, with the other lands belonging to it; also the city of Bosorran with the other lands belonging to it—two cities.
And from the tribe of Issachar, the city of Kishion with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Daberath with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Remas Bosorran with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of the Spring of Writings with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.
And from the tribe of Asher, the city of Mishal with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Abdon with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Helkath with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Rehob with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.

And from the tribe of Naphtali, the city they set apart for someone who had killed a person, Kedesh in Galilee, with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Emath Themmon with the other lands belonging to it: three cities.
All the cities of Kedson, according to their clans, amounted to thirteen cities.
And the descendants of Merari, the remaining Levites, received from the tribe of Zebulun the city of Maan with the other lands belonging to it, and Kedesh with the other lands belonging to it.
And Sella with the other lands belonging to it: three cities.

And on the bank of the Jordan at Jericho, they received from the tribe of Reuben the city of refuge for someone who had killed a person—that is, Bezer in the wilderness—and the city of Mishor with the other lands belonging to it.
And the city of Gedor with the other lands belonging to it, and the city of Phama with the other lands belonging to it: four cities.

And from the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge for someone who had killed a person, namely Ramoth in the land of Gilead, with its surrounding lands, and the city of Mahanaim with its surrounding lands.
And the city of Heshbon with its surrounding lands, and the city of Jazer with its surrounding lands—four cities in all.
All the cities given to the descendants of Merari according to their clans, those who remained of the tribe of Levi, made up their allotment of twelve cities.
All the cities of the Levites within the inheritance of the Israelites were forty-eight cities, with the lands belonging to them.

Around these cities were the lands belonging to them, surrounding each city on every side. (a) And Joshua finished dividing the land among the Israelites according to its boundaries. (b) And the Israelites gave Joshua a share according to the Lord’s command. They gave him the city he wanted to receive, namely Timnath-serah. They gave it to him in the hill country of Ephraim. (c) And Joshua built the city and lived in it. (d) And Joshua took the stone knives with which he had circumcised the Israelites who had been on the journey in the wilderness, and he placed them in Timnath-serah.
