And the Lord gave Israel all the land he had sworn to give their ancestors. They took possession of it and lived in it.
And the Lord gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of their enemies stood against them in battle. The Lord handed all their enemies over to them.
And not one of all the good promises the Lord had made to the Israelites failed; they all came true.
After these things, Joshua summoned the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the descendants of the tribe of Manasseh.
He spoke to them, saying, “You have obeyed every instruction that Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave you. You have also obeyed my voice and everything he commanded you.
You have not abandoned your fellow Israelites throughout these days and beyond them, right up to today, but you have kept the commandments of the Lord our God.

But now the Lord our God has given your fellow Israelites rest, just as he promised them. So now turn back and go to your homes and to the land of your inheritance, which Moses gave you on the other side of the Jordan.

But take great care to carry out the commandments and the law that Moses, the Lord’s servant, entrusted to you for us to carry out: that we should love the Lord our God, walk in all his ways, keep his commandments, and hold fast to him, and that you should serve him with all your soul.”
And Joshua blessed them and sent them away to go, and they went to their homes.

Moses had given half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh an inheritance in the land of Bashan, while Joshua had given the other half of the tribe of Manasseh an inheritance with their fellow Israelites near the sea. And when Joshua sent them away to their homes, he blessed them.

And they went to their homes with great wealth, with very many livestock, with silver, gold, and iron, and with many garments. They divided all the plunder from their enemies among themselves and their other fellow Israelites.

And the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh departed from the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their inheritance, which they had received by the Lord’s command through Moses.

And they came to Gilgal by the Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan. The descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh built an altar there beside the Jordan, a large altar that could be seen.

And the Israelites heard people saying, “Look, the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the borders of the land of Canaan, in the land of Gilead by the Jordan, on the side belonging to the Israelites.”
And all the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go up and fight against them.
And the Israelites sent Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
And ten other leaders went with him [?].
[?] the whole assembly of Israel. And Achan was just one man. Was he alone the one who died because of his sin?
And the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the commanders of Israel, saying to them:

“God—he himself is God; he is the Lord God. God himself knows, and Israel too will understand. If for any reason we have turned away from the Lord and sinned before him, may the Lord not save us in this.
And if we built ourselves an altar to turn away from our God, or to offer sacrifices on it—[?] or grain offerings—or to make a peace offering on it, may the Lord investigate these things.
But we did this out of fear of something, saying, ‘Otherwise, in the future your children might say to our children: What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?

The Lord established boundaries among you and among you, namely the Jordan, and you have no share in the Lord.’ Then your children would make our children outsiders, so that they would not serve the Lord.
For this reason we said we would do this: build this altar, not for sacrifices or burnt offerings.

Rather, this structure is to be a witness between us and you, and among our generations after us, that we may serve the Lord before him with burnt offerings, with sacrifices, with the other sacrifices, and with our other peace offerings. Then your children will not say to our children in the future, ‘You have no share in the Lord.’

And we said, ‘If this ever happens, and they speak this way to us or to our [?] in the future, we will say to them: Look at the replica of the Lord’s altar that our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but set up as a witness among you and among you and the other children.’
So may we never turn away from the Lord in these days by building ourselves an altar for our burnt offerings and peace offerings apart from the Lord’s altar, which stands before his tent.”

And when Phinehas the priest and all the leaders of the assembly of Israel who were with him heard these words spoken by the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were pleased.

And Phinehas the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, “Today we know that the Lord is with us, because you [?] committed a sin before the Lord, and because you have rescued the Israelites from the Lord’s hand.”

And Phinehas the priest and the leaders with him returned from the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and reported these words to them.

They pleased the Israelites, and they spoke with the Israelites and blessed the God of the Israelites. And they said that they would no longer plan to go up against them in war to destroy the land of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, where they had settled.
And Joshua named the altar of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, saying, “This altar stands as a witness among them, because the Lord God is theirs too.”
Now, after many days had passed since the Lord had given Israel rest from all its enemies around it, Joshua had grown old and was advanced in years.
And Joshua called all the Israelites, their elders, their rulers, their scribes, and their judges. He said to them, “I have grown old and am advanced in years.
You have seen what the Lord our God did to all these nations before us, because the Lord our God himself fought against them for us.

You have seen that, as I told you, [?] the nations that remain for you in the allotted territories among the tribes, from the Jordan—all the nations I drove out—and from the Great Sea, which marks your boundary toward the sunset.

But the Lord our God is the one who will drive them out before us until they are destroyed. He will send wild animals among them until he drives them and their kings out before you, and you will inherit their land, as the Lord our God told you.
Be very strong in keeping and doing everything written in the law of Moses, so that you do not turn aside to the right or to the left,
so that you do not go among these nations that remain for you. The names of their gods must not be invoked among you, and you must neither worship them nor serve them.
Instead, you must hold fast to the Lord our God, as you have done to this day.
And the Lord will drive out great and powerful nations before you. No one has stood against us to this day.
One of you chased away a thousand men, because the Lord our God fought for us, as he told us.
And you must be very careful to love the Lord our God.
For if you turn away from him and attach yourselves to these nations that remain with you, take wives from among them, and associate with them, and they in turn associate with you,

know that the Lord will no longer continue to drive these nations out before you. They will become traps and snares for you, whips against your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the Lord our God gave you.

But I am going on the path appointed for everyone on earth. You know in your heart and your soul that not a single word has failed out of all the words that the Lord our God spoke concerning every matter that affects us. Not a single one of them has proved false.

And just as all the good things that the Lord spoke to us about have come upon you, so the Lord God will bring all the bad things upon you, until he drives you out of this good land that the Lord gave you,
when you abandon the covenant of the Lord our God, which he commanded you to keep, and go and serve other gods and worship them.”
And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shiloh. He called their elders, their scribes, and their judges, and had them stand before God.

And Joshua said to all the Lord’s people, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘Your ancestors lived beyond the river long ago—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and they served other gods.
And God took our father Abraham from beyond the river, led him through all the land, multiplied his descendants, and gave him Isaac.

And to Isaac he gave Jacob and Esau. He gave Mount Seir to Esau for him to inherit it. And Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt. There they became a great nation, numerous and strong, and the Egyptians oppressed them.
And the Lord struck Egypt with the things he did among them, and afterward he brought
our ancestors out of Egypt. And you reached the Red Sea, and the Egyptians pursued our ancestors with chariots and horses into the Red Sea.

And we cried out to the Lord, and he placed a cloud and darkness between us and the Egyptians. He brought the water of the sea down upon them, and it covered them. Our eyes saw what the Lord did in the land of Egypt and in the wilderness for many days.

And he brought us into the land of the Amorites who lived across the Jordan. Moses fought against them, and the Lord handed them over to you. You took possession of their land and destroyed them before you.
And Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam and summoned him to curse you.
But the Lord your God did not want to destroy you. Instead, he blessed us abundantly and rescued us from their hands. He handed them over to us.

And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The inhabitants of Jericho fought against us, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites, and Girgashites. The Lord handed them over to us.
And he sent the locust ahead of us and drove them out before you—the twelve kings of the Amorites—not by your sword or by your bow.
And he gave you a land for which you had not labored, and cities that you had not built, and you settled in them. You ate from [?] vineyards and olive trees that you had not planted yourselves.

Now fear the Lord and serve him with uprightness and righteousness. And now remove from among you the foreign gods that your ancestors served on the other side of the river and in Egypt, and serve the Lord alone.

But if serving the Lord does not please you, then choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your ancestors who were across the river, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my household will serve the Lord, because he is holy.
And the people answered, saying, “May we never abandon the Lord and go to serve other gods!”

“For the Lord our God is God. He is the one who brought us and our ancestors up out of Egypt. He protected us along the entire road we traveled and among all the other nations through which we passed.”
“And the Lord himself drove out before us the Amorites and all the other nations living in the land. So we too will serve the Lord, for he is our God.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You will not be able to serve the Lord, because he is a holy God. And if he becomes jealous over you, he will not forgive your sins and your lawlessness.”
“When you abandon the Lord and serve other gods, and he comes against you, he will afflict you and destroy you, because he has done good for you.”
And the people said to Joshua, “No! We will serve the Lord our God.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves, because you yourselves have chosen the Lord for yourselves, to serve him.”
“Now, then, remove the foreign gods that are among you, and direct your hearts toward the Lord, the God of Israel.”
And the people said to Joshua, “We will serve the Lord and obey his voice.”
And Joshua established a covenant with the people that day. He gave them a law and a ruling at Shiloh, before the tent of the God of Israel.
And he wrote these words in a book of God's law. Joshua took a large stone and set it up under the terebinth tree, before the Lord.

And Joshua said to the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness among you, because it has heard all the words that the Lord spoke to you, since he himself spoke with you today. It will be a witness among you in the days to come if you lie to the Lord our God.” And Joshua
He sent all the people away, and each one went up to his own place.

And Israel served the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetime of the elders who had spent their time with Joshua, and the others who had seen all the works of the Lord that he had done for Israel.
And after those days, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten.

And they buried him within the boundaries of his inheritance, in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead. (a) And he placed beside him, in the tomb where they buried him, the stone knives with which he had circumcised the Israelites at Gilgal when he brought them out of the land of Egypt, as the Lord had commanded them. And they are in that place to this day.

And the bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up out of Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob had bought from the Amorites who lived in the territory of Shechem for a hundred lambs. And he gave it to Joseph as an inheritance.

And after these things, Eleazar son of Aaron, the high priest, died. His son Phinehas buried him in Gibeah, which he had given him in the hill country of Ephraim. (a) In those days the Israelites took the ark of God and carried it around among them. And Phinehas took over the priesthood in place of Eleazar his father until he died, and they buried him in Gibeah, in his own land. (b) The Israelites went away, each to his own place and his own city. And the Israelites served Astarte and Ashtaroth and the gods of the nations around them. And the Lord handed them over to Eglon king of Moab, and he ruled over them for eighteen years.
